text:
acme_ops: Hey team — after a token refresh our on‑prem Private deployment started returning intermittent 502s for calls to api.redwood.com. It works for ~30–90s then fails with SSL/TLS errors. Happening from two colo sites behind corporate proxy. Sample curl + python traceback below. Can you help triage?

jules_support: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the curl -v output and the exact error from the app? also which proxy product/version are you using?

acme_ops: here is the curl output from one host (sanitized):

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to proxy.corp:8080 (10.10.1.1) port 8080 (#0)
> CONNECT api.redwood.com:443 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.com:443\r\nProxy-Authorization: Basic XXXXX\r\n\r\n< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established\r\n\r\n* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2):
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS alert, unknown CA (256):
* SSL: certificate subject name 'proxy.corp' does not match target 'api.redwood.com'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number
```

acme_ops: python client sees SSLError: [SSL: WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER] wrong version number (_ssl.c:XXXXX) right after a token refresh requests succeed briefly then fail. Proxy is BlueCoat 12.5 with TLS inspect enabled.

jules_support: that looks like the proxy is doing TLS termination / re‑signing (MITM). when curl CONNECT returns 200, the proxy should pass a raw TLS tunnel. your trace shows the server cert is proxy.corp which explains the CN mismatch. two paths to investigate: 1) ensure CONNECT stays a pure tunnel for api.redwood.com (TLS passthrough) or 2) trust the corporate CA on the app hosts so re‑signed certs validate.

jaya_infra: additional gotcha: Redwood uses SNI for multi‑tenant routing. If the proxy rewrites the SNI or terminates TLS, the backend may see a different server_name and Redwood will reject the handshake for that virtual host (or return an unexpected cert). Also some proxies rewrite Host headers on CONNECT proxies incorrectly which breaks HTTP/1.1 Host matching after TLS tunnel.

sean_eng: can you run an openssl check from one of the failing hosts and paste output? e.g.:
```
openssl s_client -connect proxy.corp:8080 -servername api.redwood.com -prexit -ign_eof
```
we want to confirm whether the TLS session is terminated at the proxy (cert CN = proxy.corp) or passed through (cert CN = api.redwood.com).

acme_ops: ran that, output snippet: 
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=proxy.corp
   i:/CN=Corp-Inspection-CA
---
server certificate
subject=/CN=proxy.corp
issuer=/CN=Corp-Inspection-CA
---
SSL handshake has read 2106 bytes and written 325 bytes
---
```
So yes: proxy is terminating.

jules_support: ok that confirms TLS MITM. Two recommended options (ranked by minimal infra change):
- Short term workaround: add your corp inspection CA to the OS/jvm/python truststore on the Redwood client hosts so the re‑signed certs validate. This usually fixes the immediate SSL errors.
- Recommended long term: configure the proxy to allow TLS passthrough (CONNECT tunneling) for api.redwood.com and any Redwood egress ranges. That keeps SNI intact and avoids routing surprises.

jaya_infra: a couple of gotchas we see in cases like this:
- If the proxy reuses backend connections across different SNI hosts, active token refresh flows can end up on a connection where the proxy expects a different host — leads to intermittent success/fail.
- Some BlueCoat configs rewrite the SNI/Host during re‑signing; verify the proxy preserves the SNI extension.

acme_ops: both sites use the same BlueCoat cluster; we pushed adding the inspection CA to the hosts and got immediate improvement in curl — fewer SSL errors but still seeing 1/50 failures.

sean_eng: that remaining 2% failure rate may be connection reuse / pooling + proxy session pinning mixing. Two more things to check: increase client connection keepalive timeout to avoid early reuse, and capture a short pcap around a failure. if you can capture the exact sequence we can see whether the proxy is swapping the server cert mid‑session.

acme_ops: attached pcap (sanitized) — see timestamps around 12:34:55 where the app does an auth refresh and the next request fails.

jules_support: got the pcap — initial look shows the proxy closes a backend connection and the next CONNECT is routed to a different BlueCoat worker which presents a slightly different re‑signed cert (same issuer but different serial). that matches a connection‑pinning race.

sean_eng: here's a recommended short checklist to remediate: 
1) Add Corp-Inspection-CA to all host truststores (OS/jvm/python).
2) Configure proxy to exempt api.redwood.com (and any model-serving domains) from TLS inspection / re‑signing if policy allows.
3) If 2 is not possible, configure proxy to preserve SNI and honor CONNECT as pure tunnel for those hosts.
4) Tune client connection pooling: reduce max reuse, increase keepalive and add jitter to refresh timing as a mitigation.
5) If you need a quick bypass: set up a small jump host with outbound NAT and point your Private deployment's egress through that (sock5/tunnel) while you sort proxy config.

acme_ops: thanks — we'll try 1+4 immediately and open a change with proxy team for 2. we may need Redwood support for a temporary IP allowlist to make sure the proxy does not attempt to intercept traffic to those IPs. can you provide the targets to whitelist?

jules_support: we can provide the published egress IP ranges for api.redwood.com and the set of domains we use for model serving and telemetry. I'm opening a ticket (SUP-2026‑042) to attach a formal list and work with your proxy team. please include exact proxy config snippets and one failing pcap in that ticket.

deploy-bot: rollback requested for last client rollout jaya/refresh-token-v2 — canceling auto rollout to prod for clients with proxy inspection enabled.

acme_ops: appreciated. we'll follow up in the ticket and share the remediation timeline.

jules_support: thanks — action items: acme_ops to add corp CA and share proxy config + pcap in SUP‑2026‑042; jaya/sean to provide egress IP list + short docs on truststore locations for common runtimes. we'll keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
